tasks.title: Backend taxonomy source of truth
tasks.description: Expose the canonical taxonomy from a single backend module and make it the source of truth for products, profiles, and interest tags.
tasks.details: Implement backend/app/taxonomy.py with immutable constants for INTEREST_TYPES, PRODUCTS, and derived ALLOWED_TAGS. Preserve legacy CIMI Invest profiles in read/validate paths only where required by the PRD, but remove them from the UI-facing profiles list. Add GET /api/taxonomy returning {interest_types, products} with products ordered as CIMI 360, CIMI Invest, Leilão, INDIP, Feirão. Keep the module versioned in the repo and avoid hardcoding taxonomy elsewhere. Pseudo-code: `INTEREST_TYPES = [...]`; `PRODUCTS = [{key,label,profiles:[...]}]`; `ALLOWED_TAGS = set(INTEREST_TYPES) | set(all profiles from PRODUCTS) | legacy profiles`; `return JSONResponse({...})`. Ensure backend validators reference ALLOWED_TAGS so no valid tag is dropped.
tasks.testStrategy: Add pytest coverage that GET /api/taxonomy returns the exact product order and all expected profiles. Add validator tests asserting every taxonomy tag is accepted and invalid tags return 422.

subtasks.title: Define canonical taxonomy constants and allowlist
subtasks.description: Create backend/app/taxonomy.py as the single canonical taxonomy module with immutable INTEREST_TYPES and PRODUCTS constants, plus derived ALLOWED_TAGS that includes all interest types, all UI-facing product profiles, and any required legacy CIMI Invest profiles for backend read/validate compatibility.
subtasks.details: Use immutable structures where possible (tuples/frozensets or frozen dataclasses) and keep the module self-contained and versioned in the repo. Define PRODUCTS in the exact required order: CIMI 360, CIMI Invest, Leilão, INDIP, Feirão. Ensure legacy CIMI Invest profiles are excluded from the UI-facing product profile lists but still represented in the validation allowlist when needed by the PRD. Export only the canonical data needed by other backend modules and avoid duplicating taxonomy literals elsewhere.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test the module constants for immutability intent, exact product ordering, and ALLOWED_TAGS membership covering interest types, all product profiles, and legacy CIMI Invest exceptions.

subtasks.title: Expose canonical taxonomy via GET /api/taxonomy
subtasks.description: Implement GET /api/taxonomy to return the canonical taxonomy payload with interest_types and products, matching the backend source of truth and preserving the specified product order.
subtasks.details: Add a read-only API handler that serializes the taxonomy module into JSONResponse with shape {interest_types, products}. Ensure the response only exposes UI-facing product profiles, keeps products ordered as CIMI 360, CIMI Invest, Leilão, INDIP, Feirão, and does not hardcode labels or profiles in the route layer. Keep the endpoint lightweight and read-only so all consumers can rely on the shared module.
subtasks.testStrategy: API test asserting status 200, payload shape, exact product order, and that response values match the shared taxonomy module.

subtasks.title: Wire backend validators to shared ALLOWED_TAGS
subtasks.description: Refactor backend validators and any shared validation helpers to use taxonomy.ALLOWED_TAGS so valid product/profile/interest tags are accepted consistently across the backend.
subtasks.details: Replace any scattered allowlists or inline validation constants with imports from the taxonomy module. Ensure validators accept every tag in ALLOWED_TAGS and reject unknown tags with the expected validation error semantics. Keep the implementation centralized so future taxonomy changes only require updating backend/app/taxonomy.py.
subtasks.testStrategy: Validator tests for accepted taxonomy tags and 422 responses for invalid tags, plus a regression test ensuring no known tag is dropped during validation.

subtasks.title: Handle legacy CIMI Invest compatibility exceptions
subtasks.description: Preserve legacy CIMI Invest profiles only in backend read and validation paths where required, while preventing them from appearing in the UI-facing taxonomy list.
subtasks.details: Add explicit handling for legacy CIMI Invest profile values in read/validate code paths so historical data remains accepted and retrievable. Ensure these legacy values are not emitted by /api/taxonomy or any UI-oriented product/profile list. Document the compatibility boundary in code comments so the exception stays constrained to backend compatibility layers.
subtasks.testStrategy: Regression tests for legacy CIMI Invest reads and validation acceptance, alongside tests confirming those legacy labels are absent from the API taxonomy response.

subtasks.title: Add backend tests for taxonomy and validation
subtasks.description: Add backend test coverage for taxonomy ordering, API serialization, validator allowlist behavior, and legacy CIMI Invest compatibility rules.
subtasks.details: Create pytest cases that verify GET /api/taxonomy returns the exact product order and expected profiles, that ALLOWED_TAGS includes every valid tag, and that invalid tags are rejected. Include focused tests for legacy CIMI Invest read/validate exceptions and confirm UI-facing lists exclude them. Keep tests deterministic and tightly scoped to the taxonomy source of truth.
subtasks.testStrategy: Pytest suite covering endpoint response order, allowlist completeness, invalid-tag 422s, and legacy compatibility regressions.

tasks.expansionPrompt: Break down the work into: define immutable taxonomy constants and derived allowed tags, implement the /api/taxonomy endpoint, wire validators to use the shared allowlist, handle legacy CIMI Invest read/validate exceptions, and add backend tests for ordering and validation.

tasks.title: Classification storage migration
tasks.description: Add classification persistence support for the expanded product set while preserving compatibility with existing contacts and history.
tasks.details: Extend the contact classification model to support the existing single-profile-per-product behavior across five products. If the current relational structure cannot represent the new products cleanly, migrate to a jsonb column shaped like `{product_key: profile}` using an idempotent additive migration. Add a migration script that converts existing CIMI 360 and CIMI Invest records without loss, preserves legacy CIMI Invest profiles in historical reads/CSV, and rejects invalid values with 422. Keep old records readable in UI/history, but only offer current profiles in editors. Pseudo-code: `if legacy_schema_inadequate: add classification jsonb`; `migrate_row(old)->new_jsonb`; `validate(product, profile in taxonomy[product])`.
tasks.testStrategy: Use migration tests against a seeded database to verify idempotent conversion, preserved legacy reads, and 422 on invalid product/profile combinations. Add a regression test confirming existing production tags remain accepted.

subtasks.details: Inspect entity definitions, join tables, indexes, API payload shapes, and any current constraints around CIMI 360 and CIMI Invest. Document gaps for new products, historical read requirements, and whether a backward-compatible relational extension is feasible before choosing jsonb.
subtasks.testStrategy: Produce a schema assessment note with explicit pass/fail criteria for relational feasibility and backward-compatibility risks.

subtasks.details: Define the final data shape, mapping rules from old records to new structure, and how legacy CIMI Invest values are preserved in historical reads and CSV exports. Specify null/empty handling, product ordering, and how future products will be represented without additional schema churn.
subtasks.testStrategy: Validate the design against representative records and confirm it can represent all required products and legacy values losslessly.

subtasks.title: Apply additive schema changes for classification storage
subtasks.description: Implement the additive schema change required for the new classification storage model, keeping the migration safe for existing deployments.
subtasks.details: Add the new jsonb column or equivalent additive fields, along with any indexes or constraints needed for query performance and integrity. Ensure the migration is non-destructive, reversible where practical, and safe to run alongside existing production data.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run migration-up and migration-down smoke checks on a clean database and an existing schema snapshot to verify compatibility.

subtasks.details: Convert each existing row into the new product-keyed representation, preserving exact profile values and avoiding duplicate writes on re-run. Make the migration additive and repeatable, with guards that skip already-converted rows and retain original semantics for unchanged data.

subtasks.testStrategy: Add regression tests for history rendering and CSV output that confirm legacy CIMI Invest profiles remain visible while editor options exclude deprecated values.

subtasks.title: Add validation and regression tests for classification persistence
subtasks.description: Add validation and regression coverage to ensure accepted values persist correctly and invalid product/profile combinations return 422.
subtasks.details: Implement request and persistence validation against the canonical taxonomy, enforcing one profile per product and rejecting unsupported values. Cover current production tags, legacy compatibility cases, and invalid combinations across all five products.
subtasks.testStrategy: Write migration tests against a seeded database plus API validation tests for valid product/profile pairs, invalid values, and expected 422 responses.

tasks.title: Shared package composition service
tasks.description: Create the shared materials and package composition layer used by email and, optionally, WhatsApp.
tasks.details: Implement backend/app/services/package.py to assemble a message body from a template plus selected materials filtered by product and language. Add support for placeholder replacement for {nome}, {primeiro_nome}, {evento}, and {produto}, removing missing placeholders cleanly instead of leaving undefined text. Ensure only materials with URLs are included in the final package; inactive or blank-link items are excluded and previewed as omitted. Reuse this service for the current post-save email pipeline and later WhatsApp composition. Pseudo-code: `render_template(template.body, context)`; `selected_materials = materials.filter(active && url && matches product/language)`; `body += format_lines(selected_materials)`.

tasks.title: Batch ReviewCarousel package selection and dispatch
tasks.description: Implement batch mode for ReviewCarousel so each item uses the same product, language, and material selection rules as the individual flow, with sequence-level defaults in SequenceKitConfig and per-item overrides. Add batch endpoint support for a package payload per item, preselect materials by classification, and reuse the existing email dispatch pipeline.
tasks.details:
Extend the ReviewCarousel batch flow to consume a package configuration shaped consistently with the individual email kit flow: product, language, selected material IDs, and any preview metadata needed by the UI. Add SequenceKitConfig defaults for the batch context so a sequence can define the baseline product/language/material rules once, while allowing each item in the batch to override product, language, or package selection when explicitly provided.

On the frontend, update ReviewCarousel so it derives the initial selection state from the contact classification, using the same product auto-selection logic already used in the individual flow. When the contact has a single compatible product classification, preselect it automatically; otherwise keep the selector explicit. Apply the same language and material defaulting rules used by the existing package composer, including institutional materials and language-matching materials, but allow per-item overrides to persist independently for each batch row/card.

On the backend, update the batch endpoint to accept a package object per item rather than a single shared package for the whole request. Validate each item independently, resolve the effective package using item overrides first and SequenceKitConfig defaults second, then dispatch the email through the same send pipeline used for individual sends so sent history, status, timestamps, and error handling remain uniform. Preserve compatibility with existing batch requests by supporting fallback behavior when a package is omitted on an item and by rejecting malformed package shapes with clear validation errors.

Ensure the batch preview and submit path use the shared package composition service so rendered content, placeholder handling, filtering of inactive or URL-less materials, and output consistency match the individual flow. Keep logging and error messages item-scoped so one invalid item does not obscure successful sends for other items in the same batch, unless the endpoint contract requires all-or-nothing semantics.
tasks.testStrategy:
Add backend tests that submit batch requests with mixed items: one using SequenceKitConfig defaults, one overriding product/language/materials, and one omitting package entirely to confirm fallback behavior. Verify that each item is validated independently, that the effective package matches the expected precedence rules, and that all successful items are recorded through the existing email send pipeline with correct sent history fields.

Add regression tests for classification-driven preselection, especially the single-classification case and the multi-classification case where the selector must remain explicit. Add UI tests for ReviewCarousel to confirm that item-level overrides do not leak across batch rows/cards and that the displayed preview matches the shared package composer output.

Add a test that exercises invalid package payloads per item and confirms the API returns structured validation errors without breaking valid items, or a predictable all-or-nothing failure if that is the chosen contract. Finally, verify that the batch endpoint produces the same rendered email body as the individual path for the same contact, product, language, and material set.

tasks.title: Rebrand CIMI Leads com nova identidade visual
tasks.description: Aplicar o novo branding do CIMI Leads na interface e nos ativos do app, atualizando a identidade visual para os tokens teal/navy, tipografia Montserrat, logo e ícones PWA. A entrega deve cobrir os principais pontos de contato do frontend e garantir consistência visual sem quebrar fluxos existentes.
tasks.details:
Implementar a camada de identidade visual do rebrand em todo o frontend, começando pela definição centralizada de design tokens para a nova paleta teal/navy, escala de cinzas de apoio, estados de foco/hover/erro e variáveis de interface reutilizáveis. Atualizar o tema global para usar Montserrat como tipografia padrão, incluindo fallback seguro, ajustes de line-height/peso e revisão de componentes que dependam de estilos tipográficos hardcoded.

Substituir o logo atual pelos novos arquivos fornecidos, garantindo versões adequadas para header, login, favicon e demais superfícies onde a marca aparece. Atualizar o manifesto e os assets PWA com novos ícones em múltiplos tamanhos, splash/shortcut icons quando aplicável, e validar que o app continue instalável e corretamente identificado em dispositivos móveis.

Revisar componentes de alto impacto visual para aderirem ao novo sistema: botões, links, inputs, cards, badges, navegação, telas de autenticação e estados vazios. Preservar a usabilidade e contraste mínimo, ajustando tokens conforme necessidade para manter acessibilidade WCAG. Se houver suporte a modo claro/escuro, mapear o rebrand para ambos os temas sem duplicar lógica. Centralizar os assets novos em uma estrutura versionada e remover referências antigas após validação.
tasks.testStrategy:
Validar visualmente as principais telas do app para confirmar aplicação consistente da paleta teal/navy, Montserrat e do novo logo. Executar checks automáticos de build/lint para garantir que a troca de tokens e assets não introduziu regressões de compilação.

Verificar manualmente a instalação PWA em desktop e mobile, confirmando ícones e nome da aplicação corretos no manifesto, na tela inicial e no atalho do navegador. Testar contraste e legibilidade em componentes principais com inspeção de acessibilidade, incluindo estados de foco, erro e hover.

Fazer regressão dos fluxos críticos de login, navegação, cadastro/edição e telas vazias para assegurar que o novo branding não alterou comportamento funcional. Se existirem snapshots visuais ou testes E2E, atualizar as expectativas apenas para mudanças de identidade visual aprovadas.
